summary: Does the word exist as a path of adjacent (up/down/left/right) cells in the board, using each cell at most once?
mainInsight: DFS from every cell that matches the first letter, extending the match one character at a time into unvisited neighbours; mark the cell as used on the way in and unmark on the way out, and return as soon as the whole word is matched.

promptVariants: Which pattern finds a path through a grid matching a string?

options: Backtracking DFS over the 4 neighbours with a visited marker
BFS started from every cell that matches the first letter
Dynamic programming over all of the board's cell pairs
Binary search over all of the board's rows and columns
cards.answer: Backtracking DFS over the 4 neighbours with a visited marker
cards.explanation: The path must not reuse cells, so the visited state must be undone when backtracking.

incorrectOptionExplanations.BFS started from every cell that matches: BFS cannot easily forbid cell reuse per path.
incorrectOptionExplanations.Dynamic programming over all of the boar: The path-dependent visited state prevents standard DP.

promptVariants: Why must the visited mark be removed after exploring a cell?
What happens if it is not?
cards.answer: The visited set describes the cells on the CURRENT path only. A cell used on a failed path must be available again for other paths, so it has to be unmarked when the DFS returns. Leaving it marked would wrongly block valid alternative paths.
cards.explanation: Marking in place with '#' follows the same rule.

promptVariants: What is the extra space, and how does in-place marking help?
What does Word Search cost in memory and how can the visited set be avoided?
cards.answer: O(L) for the recursion (the path length). Using a visited set adds up to O(L) entries; marking cells in place avoids the set entirely.
cards.explanation: No O(mn) visited matrix is needed.

promptVariants: After `found = True` your DFS returns without popping or unmarking, and the outer loops keep starting new searches. What problems can that cause and how do you fix them?
Rewrite the DFS to return a boolean.
cards.code:
if len(path) == len(word):
    found = True
    return
for i in range(4):
    ...
    dfs(nr, nc)
path.pop()
seen.remove((r, c))
# outer loops continue after found
cards.answer: Returning early skips the cleanup, so path/seen stay polluted; later dfs calls start with stale state and may do wasted work or odd branching, and the outer loops still scan every other start cell. Make dfs return True/False, stop as soon as it returns True (`if dfs(...): return True`), and clean up after failures only.
cards.explanation: The answer is still right here only because found is monotonic.
